decisions.chose: carry as a build step in layer-tooling that injects the Git version into the API and screens (see decision-5).
decisions.reason: Chose carry over drop because decision-5 already replaces the generated version file with a build step, and the capability is a single action: stamping the Git version at build; the inputs do not say whether to keep it, so carrying it is the recommended answer. Assumes builds run in a Git checkout or CI supplies the version.

decisions.chose: carry: the service downloads, unpacks and stores Microsoft's template package (see decision-8), parsed by layer-domain and stored by layer-data.
decisions.reason: Chose carry over upload-only because the analysis lists this capability (download and unpack Microsoft's package, 6 actions) and decision-8 already carries it in layer-api; users can still upload ADMX and ADML packages (decisions 1 and 3), so dropping it would remove only the one-step fetch from Microsoft, not the way to load definitions. The inputs do not settle drop versus carry, so carrying is the recommended answer. Assumes outbound HTTPS to Microsoft is allowed.

decisions.chose: carry as a settings row in PostgreSQL exposed through the API and shown on a settings screen (see decision-4).
decisions.reason: Chose to carry it over dropping it because the policy text language drives how templates are loaded and displayed; assumes one shared row, as no sign-in exists in the inputs.

decisions.chose: carry with its sources replaced: POL file by upload and download, registry, user hive and Group Policy object sources by REG or POL import and export, and the live system source dropped (see decision-1, 2 and 7).
decisions.reason: Chose to carry the capability with file-based sources over dropping it because choosing and saving policy state is the core flow; the live registry and Active Directory sources cannot run on a server, and the owner is assumed to accept that loss.

decisions.chose: carry in full: Enabled, Disabled, Not configured with options and comment, and SPOL text in and out, with rules in layer-domain and state stored by layer-data.
decisions.reason: Chose to carry it unchanged in behaviour over redesigning it because it is the product's purpose and its rules are pure and testable in Domain; assumes the rules transfer as analysed.

decisions.chose: carry in full: filters and search by ID, text and registry key and value, with the matching rules in layer-domain and results shown by layer-web.
decisions.reason: Chose to carry it over dropping or deferring it because administrators locate policies mainly by search; chose Domain-side matching over database queries to keep the rules identical and testable, assuming template data fits in memory per request.

decisions.chose: carry: raw key and value editing of an uploaded policy file, with REG import and export, rules in layer-domain.
decisions.reason: Chose carry over drop because the analysis lists this capability (35 actions: change the raw keys and values of a policy file, REG in and out) and no input names a replacement for those actions; the inputs do not settle drop versus carry, so carrying is the recommended answer. Assumes REG round-trip fidelity is tested and that raw editing acts on the uploaded policy file stored by layer-data.

decisions.chose: carry in full: categories, products, support rules, template files and policies with detail views, built on parsed definitions from layer-domain.
decisions.reason: Chose to carry it over deferring it because every other capability selects policies from these views; it is the largest capability, so it is expected to split into several stories.
